# Pesher Psalms Column 4 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Pesher Psalms Column 4 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 4:1 — "saints" vs. "faithful ones" vs. "loyal ones"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "His saints" | Traditional rendering of *chasidav* |
| LOGOS | "His faithful ones" | More precise — *chasid* = faithful/pious |
| PNEUMA | "His loyal ones" | Modern, accessible |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "His faithful ones" — *chasidav* denotes piety/faithfulness, and "saints" carries later Christian connotations inappropriate for a Second Temple Jewish text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 4:2 — "seed" vs. "offspring" vs. "children"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the seed of the wicked-ones" | Literal *zera ha-resha'im* |
| LOGOS | "the offspring of the wicked" | Slightly more natural |
| PNEUMA | "the children of the wicked" | Modern English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the seed of the wicked" — "seed" is a deliberate biblical term (*zera*) used throughout this pesher in contrast with the "inheritance of Adam." Maintaining it preserves the agricultural/genealogical imagery.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET (with LOGOS's removal of hyphen).

---

## 4:9 — "inheritance of Adam" vs. "inheritance of humanity"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the inheritance of Adam" | Preserves proper name |
| LOGOS | "the inheritance of Adam" | Same — Adam as primordial figure |
| PNEUMA | "the whole inheritance of humanity" | Reads *adam* as common noun |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the inheritance of Adam" (EMET/LOGOS). In this eschatological context, Adam likely refers to the first human and the primordial inheritance of Eden/the land, not merely "humanity."

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 4:12 — "watches" vs. "spy on"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "watches the righteous-one" | Literal *tsofeh* |
| LOGOS | "watches the righteous" | Standard Psalm rendering |
| PNEUMA | "spy on the righteous" | Emphasizes hostile intent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "watches" (EMET/LOGOS). The Hebrew *tsofeh* means "watches/observes." PNEUMA's "spy on" imports espionage connotations beyond the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 4:16 — "Torah" vs. "law" vs. "instruction"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the Torah which he sent to him" | Preserves *torah* as loanword |
| LOGOS | "the law which he sent to him" | Standard translation |
| PNEUMA | "the instruction he had sent him" | Dynamic — *torah* as "instruction" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET "the Torah which he sent to him" — in the context of Qumran legal writings (cf. 4QMMT), *torah* carries a specific technical meaning that neither "law" nor "instruction" fully captures. Preserved as a loanword.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 4:17 — "pay him his recompense" vs. "repay him" vs. "punish the Wicked Priest"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "pay him his recompense" | Literal *yeshalem lo gemulo* |
| LOGOS | "repay him" | Concise formal |
| PNEUMA | "punish the Wicked Priest" | Explicit, dramatic |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "repay him" (LOGOS) — concise and accurate. EMET is overly literal; PNEUMA adds "the Wicked Priest" which is not in this clause.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 4:18 — "ruthless ones of the nations" vs. "violent ones" vs. "ruthless foreign powers"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "ruthless-ones of the nations" | Literal, consistent with Col. 2 |
| LOGOS | "violent ones of the nations" | Formal variant |
| PNEUMA | "ruthless foreign powers" | Dynamic condensation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "ruthless ones of the nations" — consistent with the Col. 2 ruling. PNEUMA's "foreign powers" loses the Hebrew partitive structure.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 4:12-14 — Psalm 37:32-33 — "let him be condemned" vs. "found guilty"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "let him be condemned when he is brought to trial" | Literal legal language |
| LOGOS | "let him be condemned when he is brought to trial" | Same as EMET |
| PNEUMA | "be found guilty when they stand trial" | Plural, modern legal |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted EMET/LOGOS — singular is correct per the Hebrew. "Condemned" is more precise than "found guilty" for the Psalmic *yarshi'ennu*.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

**Total disagreements for Column 4: 8**
